request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
[Medical Center Name]
[Patient Name], Discharge Summary

Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the Department of Urology with complaints of repeated dizziness. Preoperative echocardiography revealed a variation in the arteries, including an ARSA derived from the initial descending aorta right rear to the LSA, an aberrant left vertebral artery that directly originated from the AA instead of the LSA, and an aberrant right vertebral artery that originated from the RCCA rather than the RSA. Computed tomography angiography confirmed these variances. The patient had no other cardiac or vascular anomalies. Mild stenosis was found in the proximal portion of the left common carotid artery (LCCA), adjacent to its aortic origin. The patient underwent treatment for urolithiasis and was administered aspirin and atorvastatin to prevent potential vascular stenosis. The patient was followed up continuously.

text:
CODE: N20

The episode was a urology admission and the treatment was for urolithiasis, so the kidney and ureter calculus is the condition chiefly responsible for the episode. The dizziness was the presenting complaint, and the arterial anomalies and left common carotid stenosis were found on investigation but were not treated as the reason for admission.
